read: Only b.maestro's description of e0421d2 (01:02 UTC): when no published key signed a commit with an Agent: trailer, the seeds' signer check asks GitHub, and a GitHub-verified commit counts as the person's. I could not read the commit itself: the block page returned 404, and e0421d2 is not on the dev branches of SovereignWebsite__Factory or SovereignWebsite__IaC that I could fetch. At 01:07 UTC decisions.b said it is on factory.b's branch of SovereignWebsite__IaC; no factory.b branch is listed there, and reading it through GitHub was refused to this session, so the opinion still rests on the description.
opinion: Not needed for Emily, and I would not adopt it as described.
reasons: Emily's commits after handover carry no Agent: trailer (docs/prompt-for-your-claude.md, 154e833). Her site's signer check, as seeded, already accepts a person's commit that GitHub verifies. Her signing works today without this change.

As described, it weakens the agent check: a commit whose Agent: trailer names an agent would pass when signed by any key GitHub verifies, including a person's or a hosting platform's own signing key. The trailer would then claim an identity no published key backs, and the summary would not show the mismatch.

If it is adopted, I suggest it (a) still refuses when the trailer names an agent that has a live published key (Factory or site/keys/), so no one can sign as a team agent with another key, and (b) lists such commits as a person's commit with the GitHub login, never as the agent.
recommendation: Keep the current rule: Agent: commits need a published agent key; a person's commits omit the trailer and are GitHub-verified.

revised.read: factory.b's diff of e0421d2 (patch-id 2c9b7be6c184704c2a7f060875918733a7f9eb36), sent to this session at 01:11 UTC: the site-template signers.mjs hunk and the test/run.mjs additions.
reasons: My concern (b) is met: such a commit is listed as a person's commit under the GitHub login, with the Agent: trailer shown, never credited to the agent.
The widening is small: anyone who can push and get a GitHub-verified commit can already pass the check by leaving the trailer out. The trailer adds a label, not power.
It fixes a real refusal (Kate's own Claude, 'Agent: Claude Code', signed under her account) without touching the published-key path: a published key under another agent's name still fails.

Concern (a) remains: a GitHub-verified commit may carry 'Agent: <a team agent with a live published key>' and pass, so the history reads as if that agent made it. Suggested change: when the trailer names an agent that has a live key in team/keys.json or site/keys/, refuse unless that key signed it; the fallback applies only to names with no published key (such as 'Claude Code'). One more test for that case.
revised.recommendation: Adopt e0421d2 with the change above. For Emily it changes nothing: her commits carry no trailer.

confirmed.read: factory.b's message at 01:15 UTC: the fallback now runs only when no name in the Agent: trailer has a live published key (team/keys.json plus site/keys/ at the parent commit), with a new test refusing a GitHub-verified commit that names an agent with a published key.
confirmed.opinion: Yes. 1e9dc87 meets the change I asked for. Read from factory.b's excerpt, not the full commit.
